Title: SQL Injection in Product Search Route
Analysis:
The `searchProducts` handler performs a direct SQL query by interpolating the user-controlled `q` query parameter (`criteria`) into the query string:
`SELECT * FROM Products WHERE ((name LIKE '%${criteria}%' OR description LIKE '%${criteria}%') AND deletedAt IS NULL) ORDER BY name`
This completely lacks sanitization, validation, or parameterization, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary SQL statements.
Because the raw database error is passed to `next(error.parent)` and returned, as well as the results returned as JSON, this enables SQL injection (specifically Union-based and error-based SQLi).

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
GET /rest/products/search?q=apple%27%20UNION%20SELECT%201,email,password,4,5,6,7,8,9%20FROM%20Users-- HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000

Title: Path Traversal via Poison Null Byte in File Server Route
Analysis:
The file server endpoint allows arbitrary files in the `ftp/` directory (or other locations) to be read by exploiting a Null Byte Injection vulnerability.
The route handler retrieves the filename from `params.file` and checks if it ends with `.md` or `.pdf`.
However, it subsequently strips everything after `%00` (the URL-encoded null byte) via `security.cutOffPoisonNullByte(file)`.
An attacker can request a file such as `secret.txt%2500.md` (which is decoded to `secret.txt%00.md` by Express).
This passes the `.md` extension check, and is then truncated to `secret.txt` before being passed to `res.sendFile()`, allowing unauthorized access to restricted files in the `ftp/` directory (such as backup files, encryption keys, or configuration files).

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000

Title: Open Redirect via Weak Whitelist Validation (Insecure URL Matching)
Analysis:
The `isRedirectAllowed` function checks if a URL is permitted to be redirected by checking if the input URL contains any allowlisted domain in the `redirectAllowlist` Set.
Because it uses `.includes()`, an attacker can easily bypass this check by supplying a malicious URL that has the allowlisted domain anywhere in it (e.g., as a query parameter or path segment), such as `https://attacker.com?redirect=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop`.
The application's redirect endpoint will allow this redirection, resulting in an Open Redirect vulnerability.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
GET /redirect?to=https://attacker.com?r=https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:3000
